title: Deleting B, searching for C
hook: C is still in the table. Will the search still find it?

knows: linear probing: a key whose slot is taken moves to the next free slot (probing-clusters-grow)
doesNotKnow: that emptying a slot can hide keys stored past it
that a delete leaves a marker saying keep looking

misconception: Deleting from a hash table just means emptying the key's slot.
objective: The learner can explain that a linear-probing search stops at an empty slot, so a delete must leave a gone marker or the keys stored past the gap become unreachable.

claims.text: In an 8-slot table where A, B, C all hash to slot 1 and sit in slots 1, 2, 3, emptying slot 2 and searching for C probes slot 1 (A) and slot 2 (empty), stops, and reports C not found.
claims.source: Builder's node run of linear-probing search (scratchpad algo10-verify.mjs): probes [1 A, 2 empty], stop, not found.

claims.text: With a gone marker in slot 2 instead, the same search probes slot 1 (A), slot 2 (gone), slot 3 (C) and finds C in slot 3.
claims.source: Builder's node run: probes [1 A, 2 gone, 3 C], found in slot 3.

claims.text: Emptying B's slot made a gap that breaks the search for C (and any key whose probe path from its home slot crosses the gap).
claims.source: Search stops at the first empty slot (CLRS 4th ed. 11.4, open addressing search); a key stored past a slot that later became empty is never reached. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: DISPUTED: The first part holds (Demo search() stops on null; own run: probes 1 A, 2 empty, not found). But 'breaks the search for every key stored past it' is false in general: a key whose home slot is past the gap (e.g. D hashed to 3, stored in 4) is still found. Only keys whose home slot is at or before the gap and stored past it are lost. The reveal itself says only 'a gap with C past it'. Fix: reword to 'breaks the search for C (and any key whose probe path from its home slot crosses the gap)'. · Builder 2026-10-14 (W-195): reworded per pass 21; awaiting re-check. | FC pass 23 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Demo.tsx reveal para 2 now reads this sentence word for word. Demo search() stops on null; own run: probes 1 A, 2 empty, stop, C not found. The parenthetical is exactly right. Own random test (8 slots, 1-7 keys, one key deleted by emptying, 59,845 key checks): a key goes missing if and only if its probe path from its home slot to its stored slot crosses the emptied slot. 0 mismatches. CLRS 11.4 from memory, not opened; the claim rests on the derivation and the test.

claims.text: Open-addressing deletion marks the slot with a special value (DELETED) instead of emptying it, so the search keeps looking past it.
claims.source: CLRS 4th ed. 11.4 (deleting from an open-addressing table by storing DELETED instead of NIL). · Fact-check pass 19 2026-10-14: VERIFIED as the standard open-addressing method (CLRS 11.4 DELETED marker). CLRS 4e also gives a marker-free deletion for linear probing (11.5.1), so "the" method is one of two; the stage does not claim it is the only one.

claims.text: Markers pile up and slow searches, so tables get rebuilt now and then.
claims.source: CLRS 4th ed. 11.4: with DELETED markers the search time no longer depends on the load factor alone, which is why chaining is more common when keys are deleted. Rebuilding is general practice, not a CLRS claim; fact-checker to confirm wording. · Fact-check pass 19 2026-10-14: VERIFIED by derivation and own node run: deletes never make a slot empty again, so empties only fall; in a 64-slot table held at 32 keys with delete/insert churn, empty slots fell to 0 and every miss probed all 64 slots. Only a rebuild (or marker-free deletion) restores empty slots. Not a CLRS quote.

claims.text: A search can stop at an empty slot because an insert always takes the first free slot, so (with no deletes) a stored key never sits past a gap in its run; without that stop, a search for a missing key would have to check every slot.
claims.source: Knuth, TAOCP vol. 3, §6.4 Algorithm L (linear probing search/insert) and the deletion discussion; CLRS 3rd ed. §11.4 (open addressing: search terminates on an empty slot because insertion would have used it). Demo.tsx search(): stops on null. · Fact-check pass 21 2026-10-14: VERIFIED: Derivation: an insert takes the first empty slot on its probe path, so every slot from the home slot to the key was full; with no deletes no slot is emptied, so no gap appears before a stored key. Without the stop, a miss has nothing to end on before checking every slot. Knuth 6.4 Algorithm L and CLRS 11.4 from memory, not opened.

recall.question: A linear-probing table has keys X, Y, Z in slots 4, 5, 6, all hashed to 4. You delete Y by emptying slot 5, then search for Z. What happens?
options: The search stops at slot 5 and says Z is not there
The search finds Z in slot 6
recall.why: The search treats an empty slot as the end of the run. A gone marker in slot 5 would have told it to keep looking.

references.note: Open addressing: deletion with a DELETED marker
